selected_problem: Fresh-main inspection after v0.12.81 found a direct child contradiction in the new directory-intent path: a trailing-slash import such as './foo.bar/' carries explicit directory intent, but the resolver derives an apparent extension from the dotted directory basename and returns through the explicit-file branch before index inference can run. Dotted directory names are therefore incorrectly treated as file-extension intent.
decision_basis: The contradiction is fully determined by the existing directory-intent rule introduced on fresh main and does not require a new module-resolution architecture.
A trailing slash is the stronger local signal: once directory intent is explicit, a dot in the directory basename must not reclassify the target as an explicit file.
The repair only changes the precedence between two existing local predicates and leaves ordinary explicit-extension and extensionless resolution behavior intact.
changes: core/semantic-repo-graph.mjs now applies the explicit-extension exact-file branch only when directory intent is not present.
Dotted directory names with trailing-slash intent continue into the existing bounded index inference instead of being rejected as apparent files.
tests/semantic-import-target-resolution.test.mjs adds a regression for './foo.bar/' resolving src/foo.bar/index.js.
